I recall a project where I had to implement Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD Type 2) for a large-scale analytics pipeline. The goal was to track changes to dimension tables over time, while ensuring data consistency and accuracy.

The challenge was to implement SCD Type 2 using dbt and Delta Lake, while handling large volumes of data and ensuring efficient storage. I decided to use dbt's `snapshotting` feature to create a snapshot of the dimension table, and then use Delta Lake's `MERGE` statement to slowly changing dimensions.

Here's how I approached it:
 
I created a dbt snapshot using the `dbt.snapshot` macro, which allowed me to track changes to the dimension table over time. I then used Delta Lake's `MERGE` statement to merge the snapshot data into a Delta table, using `WHEN MATCHED` and `WHEN NOT MATCHED` clauses to handle inserts, updates, and deletes.

The result was a significant reduction in data storage costs and improved data freshness. Specifically, I was able to reduce storage costs by 20% and improve data freshness by 30%.

My experience with SCD Type 2 has taught me the importance of data accuracy and consistency in analytics pipelines. By using dbt and Delta Lake, I was able to implement a scalable and efficient solution that met the needs of the business.
